_comment: PH-0.10. This file implements the policy in 13 §16.1 (DEC-59, BR-1826 to BR-1829), which is
the authority — if the two disagree, the document is right and this file is a bug.
Renovate is configured but NOT yet installed: enabling the GitHub App is founder work, and
until that happens this file enforces nothing. Recorded as such rather than counted.
_scheduleComment: BR-1829 — a bounded, predictable batch gets read; a continuous trickle gets skimmed.
Monday mornings only, at most five open PRs. Africa/Cairo because 'Monday morning' means the
founder's Monday morning, and a UTC schedule would land them on Sunday night in winter.
_rangeComment: BR-1591 / DEC-46 — exact versions only. A range is how a working build breaks overnight with no code change.

_comment: BR-1827 — a security advisory PR is NEVER auto-merged, at any level, however green CI is.
Advisory patches are the class most likely to carry an urgent, lightly-tested change, and
the moment to look closely is not the moment to automate. `schedule: null` lets these

packageRules._comment: BR-1826 — devDependencies at patch and minor. A devDependency that breaks stops the build loudly and locally; it does not change what the product does in production.
BR-1826 — a devDependency major still changes tooling behaviour. TypeScript, ESLint and Vitest majors have each moved a rule or a default that this repository depends on.
BR-1826 — a runtime dependency is never merged without a human reading the diff, at ANY level. Patch releases have changed runtime behaviour before.
GitHub Actions at patch and minor auto-merge. A workflow that breaks is visible on the next push and affects nothing a user can reach.

_comment: BR-1828 — Docker base images are manual, and this is the one rule most likely to be
loosened by someone who does not know why it exists. BR-1810 requires the pinned Node
version to stay identical across engines.node, .nvmrc, packageManager, the CI matrix and
every Dockerfile. Renovate can change the Dockerfile line. Only a person can change all
five coherently, and a bump that changes one of the five is worse than no bump at all,
because the mismatch is silent until something behaves differently in production.
TypeScript is held at 6.0.3 by BR-1805: typescript-eslint declares `typescript: <6.1.0`,
and TypeScript 7 would SILENTLY disable type-aware linting — the mechanism that enforces
BR-1579. The failure mode is a green build with half its rules gone, so this is pinned
here as well as documented. Unpin when typescript-eslint supports TypeScript 7.

packageRules._comment: Node tracks LTS only (BR-1593), so odd-numbered majors never appear as a suggestion.
